name: PowerShell - Create PSCredential Object
description: Creates a PSCredential object for use with PowerView ACL abuse cmdlets. Required when running ACL abuse from a different user context (e.g., you have a compromised account's password and want to abuse that account's AD rights without changing your interactive session). Used as -Credential $Cred in subsequent PowerView calls.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY YOU NEED A PSCREDENTIAL OBJECT ===
ACL abuse in AD means you've found that USER A has an overpermissive right over
USER B or GROUP C — for example, ForceChangePassword, GenericWrite, AddSelf.
You're operating AS a different user than USER A in your current session.
PowerView's -Credential parameter lets you execute actions AS USER A without
changing your shell's actual token (no runas, no new logon session).

This is the critical setup step before ANY PowerView ACL abuse action.

=== HOW THE CHAIN WORKS ===
1. Enumerate interesting ACLs: Find-InterestingDomainAcl
2. Identify: wley has ForceChangePassword over damundsen
3. You have wley's creds — create PSCredential for wley (this card)
4. Run Set-DomainUserPassword -Credential $Cred -Identity damundsen
5. Now you control damundsen
6. damundsen has GenericWrite on Help Desk Level 1 group → add yourself
7. Help Desk Level 1 has AddSelf on IT Admins → join IT Admins
8. IT Admins has WriteDACL on domain object → grant yourself DCSync rights
9. DCSync everything

=== COMMON CREDENTIAL VARIABLE PATTERN ===
$SecPassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'transitioner' -AsPlainText -Force
$Cred = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('INLANEFREIGHT\wley', $SecPassword)

Then pass to PowerView:
  Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity damundsen -Credential $Cred ...
  Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Help Desk Level 1' -Credential $Cred ...

=== WHY THIS IS LOW-OPSEC-IMPACT ===
Creating a PSCredential object is purely in-memory — no auth events fired,
no logon sessions created until you actually USE the credential in an action.

examples.label: Create credential for damundsen after taking over

defense.why_it_works: Builds a PSCredential object in PowerShell to authenticate/run commands as a user whose password the attacker now controls (after abusing an ACL to reset it).
defense.prerequisites: Control of a target account's password (e.g. via ForceChangePassword) on a PowerShell host.
defense.impact: The ability to act as the target account for the next ACL-chain step or lateral movement.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1134] a logon (4624) as the target account from an unexpected host; PowerShell credential use (4104).
defense.artifacts: A 4624 for the target account; PSCredential creation in script-block logs.
defense.prevention: Monitor logons for accounts from unusual hosts; the upstream ACL abuse (password reset) is the primary detection point.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-privileged users or groups have been granted sensitive AD object permissions (WriteDACL, GenericAll, GenericWrite, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, etc.) through misconfigured delegation, 'inherited from parent' ACEs copied at provisioning time, or direct one-off grants. Because AD ACEs are not surfaced in the normal GUI, these often persist for years.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Example: a help-desk group has ForceChangePassword on Domain Admins members
# Found via BloodHound 'ForceChangePassword' edge, or PowerView:
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'Domain Admins' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'ResetPassword'} |
  Select-Object IdentityReference, ActiveDirectoryRights, ObjectType

# Another dangerous pattern — GenericWrite on a user (enables targeted Kerberoasting):
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'svc_sql' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite'}
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Run AD ACL audit quarterly (automated):
# BloodHound: Mark all Domain Admins as 'High Value', find paths from low-priv users
# PowerView batch:
Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDACL|WriteOwner'} |
  Where-Object {$_.IdentityReference -notmatch 'Domain Admins|Enterprise Admins|SYSTEM'} |
  Export-Csv acl_review.csv

# 2. Remove dangerous ACEs:
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'svc_sql' \
    -PrincipalIdentity 'helpdesk' -Rights GenericWrite

# 3. Enable AD Protected Users group for privileged accounts
# 4. Use tiered administration (Admin Tier 0/1/2) to limit blast radius
